label: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017
output:
D. Bergeron, and everyone else on this thread,

My nephew Thomas showed me this thread this morning. I don’t read the board every day. I was a bit angry at first, I won’t lie. Then I read it again and I thought, okay, if I did not know me, I would ask questions too. So you are right, D. Bergeron. You deserve a straight answer before the 4th. Here it is.

No, we are not closing. No, we are not moving. No, there is no condo project, no bank, no vape shop. The building at the corner was sold. I bought it.

M. Ferland is 81. He is retiring to Sherbrooke with his daughter. He offered to sell to me before anybody else. We signed at the notary on December 15. He has come every morning for 17 years for his baguette pas trop cuite. He cried a bit at the notary. I did too, a little. So Marc-Antoine, your cousin is half right: yes, the building was sold. To me. The rest of the story, the condos and the bank and the vape shop, that is not true. The bakery stays a bakery. That is the “grande nouvelle.”

About the sign: that was Thomas. He wrote it at 6h in the morning. “Grande nouvelle” was his idea. I said okay without thinking. That was my mistake. I wanted to keep the surprise for the reopening. I see now that with the carnets and the timing, a vague sign was not fair to people. I am sorry for that. I know a vague sign plus a sold building plus carnets looks bad from the outside. If I was on the outside, I would think the same.

Why we are closed from January 4 to 18: works. We are putting in a new deck oven, 4 decks, from our supplier in Laval. The old one is from 1998 and it broke three times this year. I cannot keep baking on it and pray every morning. We are also taking the space at the back, the old storage of the dépanneur. Six small tables. Finally people can sit down with a coffee and a piece of bread instead of eating in the street. We reopen for normal business Tuesday, January 19 at 7h. Then on Saturday, January 23, I am doing a small reopening, not a big ceremony. Coffee and a piece of the new bread, free, for anybody who comes. Everybody is invited. I would be happy to see you.

About the shelves on the 28th: we sold everything for Christmas Eve. 400 bûches. When you sell 400 bûches, the shelves are empty. That is not a closing sale. That is Christmas.

Now the carnets, because that is the important question and I want to be very clear. We sold 214 carnets in October. $60 for 12 loaves. All of them are still good. There is no expiry date. In January, every carnet holder gets one free croissant. Not one per loaf, one per holder, as a thank you. If somebody really wants the money back for their carnet, they can come and see me and I give it back. No question, no argument, no hard feelings. noodle_and_crumb, you said you have 7 loaves left. Bring the carnet and use it, or come and ask for the money back. Either is fine. I am not hiding from anybody. I am at the counter.

The three apartments upstairs stay rented. Same tenants, same rent. I promised them in writing. They are not being pushed out, and I am not turning them into condos. I know people worry about that in Mile End, and I understand why. I have seen many small shops close too. It is not a nice feeling. But a scam? That hurt. Seventeen years on Fairmount. I have been there since March 2009. I know half the street by name. I gave Priya’s kid a chocolatine every Saturday for a year, she can tell you. Priya, thank you for saying something. And thank you to the others who said wait, maybe there is an explanation. I saw it. It matters.

I don’t want a fight on this board. I want people to come back and see the bakery. If you were worried, I understand. If you are still angry about the sign, I understand that too. The sign was my fault, the surprise was my idea, and the bakery is not going anywhere. I bought the building so it stays a bakery. That is the whole story.

So: closed January 4 to 18. Reopen Tuesday, January 19 at 7h. Reopening Saturday, January 23, coffee and bread free. Come say hello.

Hélène
Boulangerie Le Pétrin Doré
5 rue Fairmount
